collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a deaf adult and a young adult, 18-25; in the story (name1) is deaf and uses sign)

collection.description: A deaf villager has chosen a sign name for a young workmate: ask what it means, or guess.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Everybody who knows (subject) for long enough gets a sign name, a little sign that means them, so (subject) doesn't have to spell them out every time. (friend) has been working alongside (subject.him/her) for a month and is desperate to find out what (friend.his/her) own will be. Today, at last, (subject) says (subject.he/she) has decided.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) shows it: one hand flipping over, quick, with a little shake at the end. "What is it?" asks (friend). (subject) signs and says it: "A fish flopping on the sand. Because of how you laugh." (friend) is not sure whether to be flattered. Then (friend.he/she) laughs, exactly like a fish flopping on the sand, and has to admit it's perfect.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) guesses. A wave? A bird? A leaf? (subject) shakes (subject.his/her) head at every guess, grinning wider and wider. Finally (subject.he/she) tells: it's (friend) tripping over (friend.his/her) own feet, which (friend.he/she) did on the very first day. (friend) groans. (subject) says it's a sign of affection. It is. (friend) uses it for (friend.him/her)self proudly within a week.
